41-218.r: 74th Amendment Act, 1992 → Ward Committees (population 3 lakh or more), Metropolitan Planning Committee (Art 243ZE), District Planning Committee (Art 243ZD); 'Municipal Committees' not among them.

41-219.r: Metropolitan Planning Committee (Art 243-ZE) → constitutional body; prepares draft development plan for the metropolitan area and sends it to the State Government; does not implement schemes.

41-220.r: MGNREGA → adult members of any household get at least 100 days' work; Act 2005, in force 2 February 2006, renamed 2 October 2009; started in Anantpur (Andhra Pradesh).

41-221.r: MGNREGA → Gram Panchayat plans (after Gram Sabha's recommendation), executes and implements works; new VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 got President's assent on 20 December 2025.
41-221.t: Gram Sabha only recommends; the Gram Panchayat is responsible for execution.

42-001.r: Part XVI (Arts 330-342A) → special provisions for certain classes: Art 330 SC/ST seats in Lok Sabha; Art 331 Anglo-Indian representation in Lok Sabha.

42-002.r: Art 330 → SC/ST seat reservation in Lok Sabha; Art 332 → same in State Legislative Assemblies.

42-003.r: Art 332 → SC/ST seat reservation in State Legislative Assemblies, in proportion to their share of the State's population.
42-003.t: Art 243D is SC/ST reservation in Panchayats, not State Assemblies.

42-004.r: Art 341 → President (after consulting the Governor, for a State) notifies which castes are Scheduled Castes in a State/UT.

42-005.r: Art 342 → President, after consulting the Governor, notifies Scheduled Tribes for a State/UT; Parliament can add or remove tribes by law.

42-006.r: Not correct: 'States prepare and amend SC/ST lists'. Parliament includes or excludes by law (Art 341 SCs, Art 342 STs); first lists by President's order, 1950.

42-007.r: President (not Governor) notifies Scheduled Tribes under Art 342(1), State-wise after consulting the Governor; a tribe ST in one State need not be ST in another.

42-008.r: Tanti-Tantwa → put in SC list by Bihar's 2015 notification; Supreme Court quashed it in July 2024: States cannot change the SC list under Art 341.

42-009.r: Scheduled Tribe status is religiously neutral (ST Order, 1950); SC status (SC Order, 1950, para 3) only for Hindus, incl. Buddhists and Sikhs.

42-010.r: ST criteria (not in the Constitution, but well established) → primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact with the community at large, backwardness.

42-011.r: After the 2007 amendment → 1206 Scheduled Castes; after the SC Amendment Act, 2017 → 1261; SCs are 16.6% of population (Census 2011).

42-012.r: Most Scheduled Tribe population (among options) → Madhya Pradesh; order: Madhya Pradesh > Rajasthan > Andhra Pradesh > Bihar.

42-013.r: No caste reservation in Rajya Sabha or State Legislative Councils; SC/ST seats only in Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies (book accepts a & c).

42-014.r: Art 338A → National Commission for Scheduled Tribes; Art 338 → National Commission for Scheduled Castes; split by the 89th Amendment Act, 2003.
hi: National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (राष्ट्रीय अनुसूचित जनजाति आयोग)

42-017.r: Art 338 → National Commission for Scheduled Castes; originally a Special Officer for SCs/STs; 65th Amendment Act, 1990 made it a multi-member National Commission.

42-018.r: Separate National Commission for STs → Art 338-A, inserted (and Art 338 amended) by the 89th Amendment Act, 2003.

42-019.r: National Commission for Scheduled Tribes → Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and three full-time members (one a woman).

42-020.r: Only NCST is a constitutional body (Art 338A, 89th Amendment Act, 2003; set up 19 February 2004); NHRC, NIA and NDMA are not.

42-021.r: Anglo-Indian nomination to Lok Sabha (Art 331: President could nominate two) → done away with by the 104th Amendment.

42-023.r: Art 333 → Anglo-Indian representation in State Legislative Assemblies; 104th Amendment Act, 2019 ended Anglo-Indian seats in Lok Sabha and Assemblies.

42-024.r: 104th Amendment Act, 2019 (enacted 2020) → abolished the two Anglo-Indian seats in Lok Sabha and Assemblies; extended SC/ST reservation for another 10 years.

42-025.r: NCBC Act → 1993; Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act → 1986; Persons with Disabilities Act → 1995; National Commission for Minorities Act → 1992.
42-025.c: No answer printed: the Minorities Commission year (1992) is not in List-II, so no code fits.

42-026.r: Of NCBC, NHRC, Law Commission and Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, only NCBC is constitutional (Art 338B, 102nd Amendment Act, 2018; five members).

42-027.r: 102nd Amendment → constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes by inserting Art 338B; chairperson Hansraj Gangaram Ahir (from 02-12-2022).

42-028.r: First Backward Classes Commission → appointed 29 January 1953 (inaugurated 18 March 1953); chairman Kaka Saheb Kalelkar.

42-029.r: Correct Articles: Election Commission → 324; NCSC → 338; Finance Commission → 280; NCBC → 338B (One Hundred and Second Amendment, 2018). No printed pair is correct.
42-029.c: No answer printed: none of the four pairs is correctly matched.

43-001.r: UNO founded 1945: Charter drafted at San Francisco (April-June 1945), signed by 50 nations on 26 June 1945; Poland 51st; UN Day 24 October.

43-003.r: UN Security Council → 15 members: 5 permanent (USA, France, China, UK, Russia) + 10 non-permanent elected for 2 years; Germany is not permanent.
43-003.h: P5 = 'FRUCU': France, Russia, UK, China, USA.

43-005.r: UNSC non-permanent members elected June 2020 for 2021-22: India, Ireland, Kenya, Mexico, Norway — not Canada; India's term began January 1, 2021.

43-006.r: April 2024 UNSC vote on Palestine's full UN membership: USA vetoed; Switzerland and UK abstained → 3 members rejected or abstained.

43-007.r: Only the 5 permanent UNSC members (USA, France, China, Britain, Russia) have veto power — not any member.

43-008.r: Demand for UN democratisation → mainly about the Security Council (only five permanent members); India, Brazil, South Africa press for it.

43-009.r: UN peacekeepers may use force in self-defence and in defence of the mandate; withdrawal needs a UNSC resolution; USA is the largest budget contributor (about 28%, 2020-21).

43-010.r: UN Credentials Committee → appointed by the General Assembly (not UNSC) each regular session; nine members; usually meets in November; checks all members' credentials, reports to GA.

43-011.r: UN General Assembly → may grant observer status to non-member States and inter-governmental bodies; Permanent Observers keep missions at UN HQ; based on practice since 1946, not the Charter.

43-012.r: UN's 8 good-governance traits: participation, rule of law, transparency, responsiveness, consensus, equity and inclusiveness, effectiveness and efficiency, accountability — not 'government legitimacy'.

43-014.r: Present UN Secretary-General (per book) → Antonio Guterres.

43-015.r: Ruchira Kamboj → India's first woman Permanent Representative to the UN (August 2022 to May 2024); earlier Permanent Representative to UNESCO, Paris (April 2014 to July 2017).

43-016.r: First African UN Secretary-General → Boutros Boutros-Ghali (Egypt), 6th SG, 1 January 1992 to 31 December 1996; second African → Kofi Annan.

43-017.r: Longest-serving UN Secretary-General → U Thant (Burma), 3rd SG, 3 November 1961 to 31 December 1971.

43-018.r: India's UN Permanent Representatives: Asoke Kumar Mukerji → Syed Akbaruddin → Ruchira Kamboj (August 2022-May 2024, first woman) → Parvathaneni Harish (since September 2024).

43-019.r: UN's six official languages → English, French, Spanish, Arabic, Chinese, Russian (working languages: English, French); Hindi is not one.
43-019.h: 'FACERS': French, Arabic, Chinese, English, Russian, Spanish.

43-021.r: International Mother Language Day (21 February) → proclaimed by UNESCO (not UNICEF) in November 1999; demand for Bangla as a national language was raised in Pakistan's Constituent Assembly.

43-022.r: India-sponsored UNGA resolution on multilingualism (June 2022) → mentioned Hindi, Urdu and Bengali for the first time; so 'more than one'.

43-023.r: Among Bengali, French, Japanese, Portuguese → French has most speakers (277 million) per book; overall English 1268, Mandarin 1120, Hindi 637 million lead.

43-024.r: First speech in Hindi at the UN → Atal Bihari Vajpayee (Foreign Minister), 4 October 1977; Narendra Modi spoke in Hindi on 27 September 2014.

43-025.r: Switzerland was not a UN member in 1996 (joined 10 September 2002); Iraq (1945), Libya (1955), Namibia (1990) were already members.

43-026.r: South Sudan → world's newest country, the 193rd, created 9 July 2011; capital Juba.

43-027.r: International Court of Justice → set up June 1945; headquarters at The Hague (Netherlands).

43-028.r: Indian judges at ICJ: B.N. Rau (1952-1953), Nagendra Singh (1973-1988), R.N. Pathak (1989-1991), Dalveer Bhandari (2012-2018, re-elected 2017 for 2018-2027).

43-029.r: International Labour Organisation → set up in 1919 under the Treaty of Versailles; UN specialised agency; headquarters Geneva.

43-030.r: UNCAC → the only legally binding universal anti-corruption instrument; asset return is its feature; the migrant-smuggling protocol belongs to UNTOC, not UNCAC.

43-031.r: Rule of Law Index → released by the World Justice Project (measuring rule of law since 2008).

43-032.r: Amnesty International is NOT a UN body (human-rights NGO, 7 million+ members); General Assembly, ICJ, Trusteeship Council are among the UN's six principal organs.

43-033.r: Amnesty International → global human-rights movement (7 million+ people, 150+ countries); founded 1961 by British lawyer Peter Benenson; HQ London.

43-035.r: Doctors Without Borders (Medecins Sans Frontieres) → international humanitarian NGO, founded in France; Nobel Peace Prize 1999.

43-036.r: Compulsory voting → 28 countries (Law Commission's 255th report, March 2015), often from age 18.
43-036.c: No answer printed: the book's figure (28) is not among the options.

43-037.r: White House → US President's official residence and workplace; address 1600 (not 1800) Pennsylvania Avenue; John Adams first resident, 1 November 1800; symbol of American democracy.

43-038.r: US President and Vice President are chosen indirectly by 'electors' of the Electoral College — not by members of Congress, House or Senate.

43-039.r: First primary in the US presidential race → New Hampshire (with Iowa), about a year before the election; President elected indirectly via the Electoral College.

43-040.r: Concept of a written Constitution first came into existence in the United States of America.

43-041.r: Larry Pressler → US Senator; Pressler Amendment (1986) linked US aid to nuclear non-proliferation; criticised Clinton administration's military help to Pakistan.

43-042.r: Pressler Amendments → US aid linked to nuclear capacity; Chakma refugees → Bangladesh; Perestroika → Gorbachev; 13 September 1993 → Israel-PLO agreement.

43-043.r: 'Pivot to Asia' → foreign-policy strategy of the U.S.A.

43-044.r: C.I.A. (Central Intelligence Agency) → civilian foreign intelligence service of the U.S.A.

43-045.r: Research and Analysis Wing (RAW) → India's foreign intelligence agency; set up 21 September 1968 under PM Indira Gandhi; works under the Cabinet Secretariat.
43-045.t: RAW is under the Cabinet Secretariat — not the Home Ministry, PMO or External Affairs.

43-046.r: Mossad → national intelligence agency of Israel (intelligence collection, covert operations, counter-terrorism).

43-047.r: ISI = Inter-Services Intelligence → Pakistan's premier military-run intelligence agency.
43-047.h: Spy agencies: CIA-USA, RAW-India, Mossad-Israel, ISI-Pakistan.

43-048.r: 'Fourth Estate' of democracy → the Press, for its role in nation-building.

43-049.r: Fleet Street (Central London) → historic centre of British newspapers (till 1980); last major office, Reuters, left in 2005.

43-050.r: Russian Parliament → Federal Assembly; Lower House = State Duma; Upper House = Council of the Federation (statements 2 and 3 swap them).

43-051.r: Parliaments: Japan → Diet (Imperial Diet); Sweden → Riksdag; Spain → Cortez; Poland → Sejim.

43-052.r: China's Parliament → National People's Congress (NPC): 2977 members, world's biggest; in practice a rubber stamp for the Communist Party.

43-053.r: 'Princelings' → descendants of senior Communist officials in China (the Party's 'crown princes').

43-054.r: TASS → official news agency of the Soviet Union till 1991; renamed ITAR-TASS (Russia) from 1992.

43-055.r: China's news agency → New China News Agency.

43-056.r: Dawn → leading English newspaper of Pakistan; founded by Mohammad Ali Jinnah in Delhi on 26 October 1941.

43-059.r: Nehru on India's Commonwealth membership → 'an agreement by free will, to be terminated by free will'.

43-060.r: First Indian PM to visit Afghanistan → Jawaharlal Nehru (September 1959); then Indira Gandhi (1976); Narendra Modi visited on June 4, 2016.

43-061.r: Non-Alignment policy → started by Jawaharlal Nehru as interim PM: stay away from international power blocs and keep an independent foreign policy.
